title: Risk Governance Panel Role Play and Delivering the Outcome
summary: Groups take turns presenting their full risk assessment and sitting as the panel, then practise explaining the outcome to the firm's board, drawing together all three days.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Groups take turns presenting their full risk assessment and sitting as the panel, then practise explaining the outcome to the firm's board, drawing together all three days.
Learning Objectives: Present a supervisory assessment concisely and seek the panel's advice
Give and respond to constructive, evidence-based challenge
Communicate ratings and required actions clearly to a firm's board
Syllabus: Mock panels: chair, members, secretary and presenting team roles
Good challenge, fair concession and pushing back on the panel
Minutes, agreed actions and comparison with a model letter
Workshop: delivering the risk assessment letter to the board
Intended Audience: Line supervisors and supervisory analysts who carry out firm risk assessments and on-site visits
Senior supervisors and team leaders who present to, chair or sit on risk governance and thematic review panels
Specialists from risk, financial crime and policy teams who contribute to firm assessments and panels
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising regulated firms is helpful. No specialist financial or interviewing background is required.
Core Reading: IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
